questions.stem: What is FaaS (Function as a Service) about?
options: Deploying ONLY functions in the Cloud and paying for the resources needed to run them
questions.explanation: FaaS is about deploying only functions in the Cloud and paying only for the resources required to run those functions.

questions.stem: How is FaaS positioned relative to CaaS in the cloud rental hierarchy?
options: At the same level as CaaS
questions.explanation: FaaS is described as one level lower than CaaS for renting resources on the Cloud.

questions.stem: Which long-standing challenge does breaking a code set into functions help mitigate?
options: Having to redeploy the whole code set whenever a requirement changes
questions.explanation: Whenever a requirement changes the whole code set traditionally had to be redeployed because of dependencies; smaller functions let only the changed code be redeployed.

questions.stem: Under FaaS, who manages the infrastructure beneath the deployed functions?
questions.explanation: Customers deploy only their functions and the infrastructure underneath is managed by the Cloud providers.

questions.stem: In which kind of workload is it acknowledged that breaking code into functions might be difficult?
questions.explanation: The topic agrees that in Data Pipelines it might be difficult, but says the option is still worth using wherever possible.

questions.stem: Which example module is described as being built from multiple functions?
questions.explanation: Referring to the CaaS example, a user authentication module built from multiple functions can have individual functions deployed at any time.

questions.stem: How does FaaS help multiple Agile teams working in silos?
options: By letting teams develop and deploy their functions at any time using CI/CD in production
By forcing a single monthly release
By merging all teams into one
By eliminating the need for testing
questions.explanation: Different teams are able to develop and deploy their own functions at any time using CI/CD in production.

questions.stem: What benefit does deploying smaller pieces of code bring, according to the FaaS description?
options: Increased flexibility to deploy only what changed, every time the code changes
questions.explanation: Being able to deploy functions at any time breaks down deployment activities and increases the flexibility to deploy a smaller piece of code whenever it changes.

questions.stem: Which statement about FaaS is FALSE?
options: The customer pays for the resources required to run the functions
It supports Agile teams deploying independently
It is one level lower than CaaS
The customer must manage the underlying infrastructure
questions.explanation: FaaS saves the customer from managing infrastructure in the Cloud; the provider manages it underneath the functions.

questions.stem: What do IaaS and CaaS rent, in contrast to FaaS?
questions.explanation: IaaS and CaaS rent infrastructure and container-level resources on the Cloud; FaaS moves to deploying functions only.
